interestRateConverterPage.title: Monthly and Annual Interest Rate Converter
interestRateConverterPage.metaDescription: Convert monthly interest rates to annual and annual to monthly using compound interest. Free and accurate tool.
interestRateConverterPage.intro: Convert monthly interest rates to annual rates and annual rates to monthly rates automatically and accurately using compound interest — the same method used by banks and financial institutions. This converter is ideal for comparing mortgages, investments, rents, loans, and any contract using interest rates over different periods. Simply enter the rate in one field to instantly see the equivalent rate for the other period, without manual calculations or incorrect approximations.
interestRateConverterPage.supportingText: Unlike simplified conversions that merely multiply or divide the rate by 12, this tool considers the real effect of compound capitalization, ensuring correct and reliable results. For example, a 1% monthly rate is not equivalent to 12% per year, but rather 12.6825% per year. If you are analyzing a mortgage, rent adjustment, investment return, or any financial simulation, this converter helps standardize rates and make more informed decisions.
interestRateConverterPage.educationalNote: Note: Conversions use compound interest. A monthly rate of 1% is not equivalent to 12% per year.

items.question: How to convert monthly interest to annual?
items.answer: The compound interest formula is used, raising the monthly rate to the 12th power to get the effective annual rate: i_a = (1 + i_m)^12 - 1.

items.question: Does this converter use simple interest?
items.answer: No. All conversions use compound interest, reflecting real financial market practices.

igpm.title: IGP-M Today: Complete History, Charts, and Rent Adjustment
igpm.description: The IGP-M (General Market Price Index) is one of Brazil's most important economic indicators, widely used for adjusting rent contracts, school tuitions, energy bills, and various services.
igpm.pageDescription: On Kitnets.com, track IGP-M updated monthly, with complete historical data since 01/01/1995, interactive charts, monthly heatmap, and detailed tables for accurate and reliable analysis.

sections.title: What is IGP-M?
sections.text: The IGP-M is an inflation index calculated monthly by Fundação Getulio Vargas (FGV). It measures price variation at different economic stages, from production to final consumption, which explains its high sensitivity to exchange rates, commodities, and global economic shocks. Due to this scope, the index became known as 'rent inflation', being the reference for millions of contracts in Brazil.

sections.title: How is IGP-M calculated?
sections.text: The calculation of IGP-M is based on a weighted average of three sub-indices, each representing a distinct stage of the economy:

items.title: 📦 IPA – Broad Producer Price Index (60%)
items.text: Monitors wholesale prices, with strong influence from agricultural commodities, industrial goods, and exchange rate variations.

items.title: 🛒 IPC – Consumer Price Index (30%)
items.text: Tracks price variation of goods and services consumed by families.

items.title: 🏗️ INCC – National Construction Cost Index (10%)
items.text: Reflects costs of materials, labor, and services in civil construction.

items.title: 📅 Collection period
items.text: From the 21st of the previous month to the 20th of the reference month, allowing for faster capture of recent price variations.

sections.title: IGP-M Today: track in real time
sections.text: On Kitnets.com's IGP-M page, you find:

items.title: Intuitive Visualization
items.text: All this in one place, with clear data and intuitive visualization.

sections.title: IGP-M History since 1995
sections.text: Kitnets.com provides one of the most complete historical IGP-M series, ideal for analyzing old contracts, simulating rent adjustments, economic and academic studies, and real estate investment decisions. You can explore the index evolution over decades and identify cycles of rise, stability, and deflation.

sections.title: IGP-M Evolution Chart
sections.text: The interactive chart allows you to visualize monthly index variation, periods of high inflation, deflation phases, and the impact of economic crises and global cycles. This visualization facilitates understanding the index behavior over time.

sections.title: IGP-M Monthly Heatmap
sections.text: The heatmap presents IGP-M behavior month by month, year by year, with intuitive colors helping to quickly identify high inflation months, deflation periods, seasonal patterns, and index volatility. It is a powerful tool for analyzing contract adjustments and historical trends.

sections.title: IGP-M and Rent Adjustment
sections.text: IGP-M is widely used in rental contracts in Brazil. Its impact is direct: high inflation leads to more aggressive adjustments, while deflation can lead to reduced or even negative adjustments. Therefore, tracking the index is essential for owners, tenants, real estate agencies, and investors who want to negotiate contracts fairly and informed.

sections.title: IGP-M or IPCA: which is better?
sections.text: In recent years, many contracts have switched from IGP-M to IPCA due to IGP-M's high volatility, especially during periods of exchange rate and commodity shocks. On Kitnets.com, you can easily compare different indices and understand which makes more sense for each type of contract.

sections.title: Why track IGP-M on Kitnets.com?
list: ✔ Ideal tool for renting and investing
✔ Focus on Brazilian real estate market

igpm.closing: IGP-M remains one of the most relevant indices in the Brazilian economy, especially for the real estate market. Understanding its composition, following its evolution, and analyzing its impacts is fundamental to avoid surprises in contracts and investments.
igpm.cta: On Kitnets.com, you find all IGP-M information in one place, with transparency, historical depth, and visual tools that facilitate decision making.

selic.title: Selic Rate: Complete History Since 1995 and Copom Decisions
selic.description: The Selic Rate is Brazil's main monetary policy instrument and directly influences interest rates, inflation, credit, investments, and economic growth. All interest rates in the country — from real estate financing to fixed income investments — have the Selic as their central reference.
selic.pageDescription: On this Kitnets.com page, you can follow the complete historical series of the Selic Rate since January 1995, the starting point of the Real Plan, with up-to-date data, interactive charts, monthly heatmaps, and detailed tables for short, medium, and long-term analysis.

sections.title: What is the Selic Rate?
sections.text: The Selic is the basic interest rate of the Brazilian economy, defined by the Central Bank of Brazil. It represents the average rate of one-day financing backed by federal government bonds, traded in the Special System for Settlement and Custody (Selic).
sections.footer: In practice, the Selic serves to:
list: Define the attractiveness of fixed income versus other assets

sections.title: Selic Historical Series Since the Real Plan (1995)
sections.text: Kitnets.com provides the Selic historical series since January 1995, allowing analysis of:
list: Interest rate behavior across different governments
Cycles of inflation fighting and economic stimulus
Periods of structurally high and low interest rates
The impact of Selic on investments, real estate, and fixed income
sections.footer: This long history is essential to understand how monetary policy has shaped the Brazilian economy in recent decades.

sections.title: Copom Decisions: How Selic is Defined
sections.text: The Selic Rate is defined by the Monetary Policy Committee (Copom), a Central Bank body responsible for establishing the basic interest rate at each cycle of meetings. Copom meets eight times a year and, at the end of each meeting, announces the new Selic target, along with a statement explaining the rationale for the decision.

sections.title: Copom Meeting Calendar – 2026
sections.text: According to the Central Bank, the official calendar for Copom meetings in 2026 is as follows:
sections.footer: 📌 The Copom minutes are published at 8:00 AM on the Tuesday following each meeting, providing a more detailed analysis of the economic scenario, inflation, economic activity, and risks considered by the committee.

sections.title: How to Interpret Selic Data on Kitnets.com
sections.text: On this page you will find:
list: Monthly heatmap, facilitating identification of high or low interest rate periods
Complete historical table, with month-by-month data since 1995
sections.footer: These visualizations help investors, property owners, and analysts understand the impact of Selic on financing, yields, and long-term decisions.

sections.title: Selic, CDI, and Real Estate Market
sections.text: The Selic directly influences the CDI, real estate financing, government bonds (Tesouro Selic), and the cost of credit for families and companies. In periods of high Selic, fixed income tends to compete strongly with real estate investments; in cycles of decline, real estate credit becomes more accessible and the property market gains traction. Therefore, following the Selic is fundamental for financial planning, investment analysis, and real estate market decisions.

The Selic historical series since the Real Plan, combined with charts, filters, and detailed tables, allows for a complete analysis of the past, present, and possible future scenarios.
